about: Native-integration capabilities of the framework versions used in this repository. 'docs' cells cite upstream documentation or release notes; 'repo' cells are backed by this repository's lockfiles, examples, captures or runner checks. Light/dark following was tested on GitHub runners by switching the OS to dark mode and relaunching each example. Other capabilities describe the current upstream release line; the Linux runs used Ubuntu 24.04's GTK 4.14 and Qt 6.4.

frameworks.name: egui / eframe
frameworks.model: Immediate mode; draws its own widgets with OpenGL or wgpu
strengths: Very little code for tool-style UIs; state lives in plain Rust fields
Screen-reader support through AccessKit on all three systems
limits: Same custom look on every OS
Menus, tray, dialogs and notifications come from separate crates
Did not follow dark mode on Linux X11

frameworks.name: GTK4
frameworks.model: Retained widget tree styled by the GTK theme (Adwaita)
strengths: Native look and system integration on GNOME/Linux
Mature text stack (Pango) with bidi and IME
Smallest executables here; the GTK runtime is separate
limits: Looks like GTK, not like Windows or macOS
Did not follow system dark mode on any runner
Windows/macOS screen-reader backend is new and opt-in
No tray icon API; runtime must be bundled on Windows/macOS

frameworks.name: Slint
frameworks.model: Declarative .slint markup compiled to native code; own renderer
frameworks.license: GPL-3.0, royalty-free with attribution, or commercial
strengths: Smallest measured memory on every system
Followed system dark mode on all three runners
Built-in tray icon and native menu bar on Windows/macOS
limits: Drag and drop works only inside the app in 1.17–1.18
No built-in file dialog or notifications
Read the licence options before shipping closed-source

frameworks.name: Qt Widgets
frameworks.language: C++ here; Rust only via bridges such as CXX-Qt
frameworks.model: Retained C++ widget tree drawn with platform styles
strengths: Closest to native controls on Windows and macOS
Broadest built-in OS integration: dialogs, tray, menus, accessibility
Low measured memory on all three systems
limits: C++ API; Rust bindings target QML rather than Widgets
LGPL obligations or a commercial licence

frameworks.name: Tauri
frameworks.model: System webview (WebView2, WKWebView, WebKitGTK) driven by Rust
strengths: Any web UI stack; official plugins for dialogs, notifications, updates
Built-in bundler for installers on all three systems
limits: Highest measured memory on Linux and Windows: the webview runs extra processes
Different browser engine on each OS
Dark mode needs the app’s own CSS

features.title: Native-looking controls
features.description: Do buttons, lists and inputs look like the platform's own controls?

egui.note: egui draws its own style, identical on every OS.

gtk.note: Native on GNOME. On Windows and macOS it keeps the GTK theme rather than platform controls.

slint.note: Built-in styles imitate Fluent, Cupertino and Material; the native style renders through Qt when the Qt backend is used. Controls are drawn by Slint.

qt.note: Platform styles on Windows and macOS; on Linux the look depends on the desktop's Qt platform theme (Fusion by default).

tauri.note: Layout and styling come from the app's CSS. Form controls and scrollbars follow the webview's defaults.

features.title: Follows system light/dark
features.description: Tested: the OS was switched to dark mode and each example relaunched.

egui.note: Followed the OS on Windows and macOS (ThemePreference::System). On Linux X11 it stayed light although the Settings portal reported prefer-dark.

gtk.note: Stayed light on every runner: GTK 4.24 on Windows/macOS and GTK 4.14 with the Linux portal set to prefer-dark. GTK 4.20+ documents gtk-interface-color-scheme for Linux; libadwaita apps follow the portal.

slint.note: The std-widgets style switched to dark on Windows, macOS and Linux (portal).

qt.note: Switched on macOS (Qt 6.12). Stayed light on Windows Server 2022 with Qt 6.8.3 and on Linux with Qt 6.4, which predates QStyleHints::colorScheme (6.5).

tauri.note: All three webviews reported prefers-color-scheme: dark. The app must style dark mode itself; the example defines both palettes in CSS.

features.title: Native Wayland and X11
features.description: Runs natively on both Linux display protocols.

egui.note: Through winit. The measured example enables only the x11 feature on Linux.

gtk.note: Wayland and X11 backends are part of GTK.

slint.note: Through winit, plus a LinuxKMS backend without a compositor.

features.title: Screen readers
features.description: Exposes the UI to Narrator/NVDA, VoiceOver and Orca.

egui.note: AccessKit adapters for Windows, macOS and AT-SPI are in the pinned lockfile (eframe feature accesskit).

gtk.note: AT-SPI on Linux. GTK 4.18 added an AccessKit backend for Windows/macOS; it is enabled at build time and selected with GTK_A11Y=accesskit.

slint.note: AccessKit adapters for all three systems are in the pinned lockfile (feature accessibility).

tauri.note: Provided by the system webview; quality depends on the app's HTML semantics.

features.title: Input methods (CJK, dead keys)
features.description: Composes text through the OS input method.

gtk.note: GtkIMContext with platform modules (IBus/Wayland text-input, Win32 IMM, macOS).

features.title: Right-to-left and bidi text
features.description: Arabic/Hebrew shaping, bidi reordering and mirrored layouts.

egui.note: Bidi shaping and RTL layout are open pull requests after 0.37.

gtk.note: Pango shaping and bidi; widgets mirror with the text direction.

slint.note: The pinned lockfile includes Parley and unicode-bidi for shaping. Automatic layout mirroring was not verified.

qt.note: Text shaping plus Qt::RightToLeft layout direction.

tauri.note: HTML dir and CSS logical properties.

features.title: Native menu bar
features.description: Uses the macOS global menu bar and native Windows menus.

egui.note: No menu-bar integration; the muda crate can add native menus.

gtk.note: gtk_application_set_menubar uses the macOS menu bar; elsewhere it is an in-window GTK menu.

slint.note: MenuBar uses the macOS menu bar and native Windows menus (muda, since 1.10); on Linux it is drawn by Slint.

qt.note: QMenuBar maps to the macOS global menu bar.

features.title: System tray icon
features.description: Notification-area or menu-bar status icon with a menu.

egui.note: Not built in; the tray-icon crate is the usual choice.

slint.note: SystemTrayIcon since 1.17. Linux uses StatusNotifierItem; plain X11 trays are not supported.

tauri.note: Core API behind the tray-icon feature.

features.title: Native file dialogs
features.description: Open/save dialogs provided by the OS or desktop portal.

egui.note: Not built in; rfd provides native dialogs.

gtk.note: GtkFileDialog uses Win32/macOS dialogs and the XDG portal.

slint.note: Not built in; rfd is commonly used.

qt.note: QFileDialog uses native dialogs by default.

features.title: Desktop notifications
features.description: Toasts in the OS notification centre.

egui.note: Not built in; notify-rust or platform crates.

gtk.note: GNotification through GApplication; Linux uses the portal or freedesktop service. Windows/macOS backends were not verified.

qt.note: Qt Widgets has no notification-centre API; QSystemTrayIcon::showMessage shows a tray balloon.

features.title: Drag and drop with other apps
features.description: Accepts drops from, and drags to, the file manager and other apps.

egui.note: Receives dropped files; dragging out of the app is not built in.

slint.note: DragArea/DropArea work inside the application; cross-app drag and drop awaits winit support.

qt.note: QDrag and drop events with MIME data.

tauri.note: Drag-drop events for files dropped on a window; dragging out needs a community plugin.

egui.note: Viewports open native windows on desktop backends.

slint.note: Each component with a Window root can be shown separately.

tauri.note: WebviewWindow; each window hosts a webview.

features.title: Installers and updates
features.description: Official tooling to produce installers and deliver updates.

egui.note: General Rust packagers such as cargo-packager.

gtk.note: Flatpak and distro packages on Linux. On Windows/macOS the GTK runtime must be collected and bundled by the app; this repository copies the MSYS2 runtime.

qt.note: windeployqt/macdeployqt collect the runtime; installers via Qt Installer Framework. No built-in updater.

tauri.note: Built-in bundler (MSI/NSIS, .app/.dmg, deb/rpm/AppImage) and an official updater plugin.

slint.text: Embedded MCUs, Linux KMS, Android, WebAssembly

qt.text: Android, iOS (Qt Quick preferred there), embedded Linux

features.title: Rust API
features.description: How a Rust application talks to the toolkit.

tauri.text: Rust core; UI in web code
